title: Rigveda 5.79: To Usas
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.79: To Usas: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.79 is a hymn of 10 verses addressed to Usas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 393v-394v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.79.1-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 393v
translation.original_text:
1ma̱he no̍ a̱dya bo̍dha̱yoṣo̍ rā̱ye di̱vitma̍tī | yathā̍ cin no̱ abo̍dhayaḥ sa̱tyaśra̍vasi vā̱yye sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
2yā su̍nī̱the śau̍cadra̱the vy auccho̍ duhitar divaḥ | sā vy u̍ccha̱ sahī̍yasi sa̱tyaśra̍vasi vā̱yye sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
3sā no̍ a̱dyābha̱radva̍su̱r vy u̍cchā duhitar divaḥ | yo vy auccha̱ḥ sahī̍yasi sa̱tyaśra̍vasi vā̱yye sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
translation.text:
1O HEAVENLY Dawn, awaken us to ample opulence to-day Even as thou hast wakened us with Satyaṣravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
2Daughter of Heaven, thou dawnedst on Sunîtha Ṣuchadratha's son, So dawn thou on one mightier still, on Satyaṣravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
3So, bringing treasure, dawn to-day on us thou Daughter of the Sky, As thou, O mightier yet. didst shine for Satyaṣravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 393v (numbered 66v by the scribe) (OPenn image 394, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.78.8 ‹-jarāyuṇā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 394r (numbered 67r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.79.4 ‹-dāman-vantaḥ su-rātayaḥ su-jāte aśva-sūnṛte›. Verses 5.79.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1mahe | naḥ | adya | bodhaya | uṣaḥ | rāye | divitmatī | yathā | cit | naḥ | abodhayaḥ | satya-śravasi | vāyye | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte
2yā | su-nīthe | śaucat-rathe | vi | aucchaḥ | duhitaḥ | divaḥ | sā | vi | uccha | sahīyasi | satya-śravasi | vāyye | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte
3sā | naḥ | adya | ābharat-vasuḥ | vi | uccha | duhitaḥ | divaḥ | yo iti | vi | aucchaḥ | sahīyasi | satya-śravasi | vāyye | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte

translation.original_ref: RV 5.79.4-7 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 394r
translation.original_text:
4a̱bhi ye tvā̍ vibhāvari̱ stomai̍r gṛ̱ṇanti̱ vahna̍yaḥ | ma̱ghair ma̍ghoni su̱śriyo̱ dāma̍nvantaḥ surā̱taya̱ḥ sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
5yac ci̱d dhi te̍ ga̱ṇā i̱me cha̱daya̍nti ma̱ghatta̍ye | pari̍ ci̱d vaṣṭa̍yo dadhu̱r dada̍to̱ rādho̱ ahra̍ya̱ṁ sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
6aiṣu̍ dhā vī̱rava̱d yaśa̱ uṣo̍ maghoni sū̱riṣu̍ | ye no̱ rādhā̱ṁsy ahra̍yā ma̱ghavā̍no̱ arā̍sata̱ sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
7tebhyo̍ dyu̱mnam bṛ̱had yaśa̱ uṣo̍ magho̱ny ā va̍ha | ye no̱ rādhā̱ṁsy aśvyā̍ ga̱vyā bhaja̍nta sū̱raya̱ḥ sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
translation.text:
4Here round about thee are the priests who laud thee, Bright One, with their hymns, And men with gifts, O Bounteous Dame, splendid with wealth and offering much, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
5Whatever these thy bands perform to please thee or to win them wealth, E'en fain they gird us round and give rich gifts which ne'er are reft away, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
6Give to these wealthy patrons fame, O affluent Dawn, with hero sons, To these our princes who have brought rich gifts ne'er to be reft away, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!
7Bring lofty and resplendent fame, O thou munificent Dawn, to these Our wealthy patrons who bestow rich gifts on us of steeds and kine, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

4abhi | ye | tvā | vibhāvari | stomaiḥ | gṛṇanti | vahnayaḥ | maghaiḥ | maghoni | su-śriyaḥ | dāman-vantaḥ | su-rātayaḥ | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte
5yat | cit | hi | te | gaṇāḥ | ime | chadayanti | maghattaye | pari | cit | vaṣṭayaḥ | dadhuḥ | dadataḥ | rādhaḥ | ahrayam | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte
6ā | eṣu | dhāḥ | vīra-vat | yaśaḥ | uṣaḥ | maghoni | sūriṣu | ye | naḥ | rādhāṃsi | ahrayā | magha-vānaḥ | arāsata | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte
7tebhyaḥ | dyumnam | bṛhat | yaśaḥ | uṣaḥ | maghoni | ā | vaha | ye | naḥ | rādhāṃsi | aśvyā | gavyā | bhajanta | sūrayaḥ | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte

translation.original_ref: RV 5.79.8-10 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 394v
translation.original_text:
8u̱ta no̱ goma̍tī̱r iṣa̱ ā va̍hā duhitar divaḥ | sā̱kaṁ sūrya̍sya ra̱śmibhi̍ḥ śu̱kraiḥ śoca̍dbhir a̱rcibhi̱ḥ sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
9vy u̍cchā duhitar divo̱ mā ci̱raṁ ta̍nuthā̱ apa̍ḥ | net tvā̍ ste̱naṁ yathā̍ ri̱puṁ tapā̍ti̱ sūro̍ a̱rciṣā̱ sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
10e̱tāva̱d ved u̍ṣa̱s tvam bhūyo̍ vā̱ dātu̍m arhasi | yā sto̱tṛbhyo̍ vibhāvary u̱cchantī̱ na pra̱mīya̍se̱ sujā̍te̱ aśva̍sūnṛte ||
translation.text:
8Bring us, O Daughter of the Sky, subsistence in our herds of kine, Together with the sunbeams, with the shine of pure refulgent flames, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!
9O Daughter of the Sky, shine forth; delay not to perform thy task. Let not the Sun with fervent heat consume thee like a robber foe, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!
10So much, and more exceedingly, O Dawn, it suits thee to bestow, Thou Radiant One who ceasest not to shine for those who sing thy praise, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!

8uta | naḥ | go--matīḥ | iṣaḥ | ā | vaha | duhitaḥ | divaḥ | sākam | sūryasya | raśmi-bhiḥ | śukraiḥ | śocat-bhiḥ | arci-bhiḥ | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte
9vi | uccha | duhitaḥ | divaḥ | mā | ciram | tanuthāḥ | apaḥ | na | it | tvā | stenam | yathā | ripum | tapāti | sūraḥ | arciṣā | su-jāte | aśva-sūnṛte
